objective: Framebuffer mmap-style shared pages and GPU viewport scrolling
method: Sequential private QEMU instances, two rounds per comparison, one raw VNC round; no concurrent regression guests; fixed scroll benchmark bypasses PTY/pacing. Timings include scheduling. QEMU CPU covers the whole command including initialization and reports.
limitations: This is a device-specific mapping API, not general POSIX file mmap.
GPU transfer/QEMU/VNC still perform work; zero-copy refers to user-to-kernel pixels.
Only two rounds; no universal throughput or frame-rate guarantee.
2000-line burst elapsed time did not improve; preserve this counterexample.
Resource retains a conservative maximum width, so a previously wide/colored row can widen future transfers.
Mappings share one display resource; applications coordinate concurrent drawing.
No VirGL, vertical synchronization, or atomic page flip.
